rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed report says Thaqif conditioned entry into Islam on exemptions from levies, military mustering, and prayer collection; keeping their usury and the Lat idol; and control of Wajj valley.
rows.anchor: لا نعشر ؛ ولا نحشر ، ولا نجبي في صلاتنا ، وكل ربا لنا فهو لنا

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: When Thaqif pressed the scribe to add that they would not collect prayer dues, Umar drew his sword and condemned their attempt to inflame the Prophet’s heart.
rows.anchor: فقام عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه فسل سيفه وقال : أسعرتم قلب نبينا يا معشر ثقيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reported occasion is Quraysh asking Muhammad to exchange mercy verses for punishment verses and vice versa so they would believe.
rows.anchor: وروي أن قريشا قالوا له : اجعل آية رحمة آية عذاب ، وآية عذاب آية رحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In wa-in kādū, in is lightened from the emphatic particle and the lām distinguishes it from a negative construction.
rows.anchor: إن مخففة من الثقيلة ، واللام هي الفارقة بينها وبين النافية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fitna here means nearly deceiving or tempting the Prophet away from the revelation, including its commands, prohibitions, promises, and threats.
rows.anchor: قاربوا أن يفتنوك أي يخدعوك فاتنين { عن الذى أوحينا إليك } من أوامرنا ونواهينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The requested fabrication was to reverse promise and threat or attribute to God what He had not revealed, as Thaqif proposed.
rows.anchor: لتفترى علينا } لتقول علينا لم لم نقل ، يعني ما أرادوه عليه من تبديل الوعد وعيدا والوعيد وعدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Had he followed their wishes, they would have taken him as an intimate ally, and he would have left God's protection and allegiance.
rows.anchor: أي ولو اتبعت مرادهم لاتخذوك { إبراهيم خليلا } ولكنت لهم وليا وخرجت من ولايتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's strengthening and protection kept him from leaning toward them; the near-leaning is a divine warning and a favor to believers.
rows.anchor: ولولا تثبيتنا لك وعصمتنا { لقد كدت تركن إليهم } لقاربت أن تميل إلى خدعهم ومكرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threatened doubled punishment is punishment of worldly life and the afterlife, with the afterlife punishment comprising grave torment and Hell.
rows.anchor: لأذقناك عذاب الآخرة وعذاب القبر مضاعفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is syntactically compressed: two punishments, each doubled, become two genitive phrases after the descriptive noun is omitted.
rows.anchor: أصل الكلام : لأذقناك عذابا ضعفا في الحياة ، وعذابا ضعفا في الممات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation takes the first doubled punishment as worldly torment and the second as grave and Hell torment after death.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد بضعف الحياة : عذاب الحياة الدنيا ، وبضعف الممات : ما يعقب الموت من عذاب القبر وعذاب النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat's severity despite describing only a near, slight yielding shows that wrongdoing grows more grave with the actor's rank; Zamakhshari invokes this against attributing evil acts to God.
rows.anchor: وفي ذكر الكيدودة وتقليلها ، مع إتباعها الوعيد الشديد بالعذاب المضاعف في الدارين دليل بين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even the least accommodation of corrupt people opposes God, leaves His protection, and warrants His anger and punishment; reciters should feel awe and strengthen their faith.
rows.anchor: أدنى مداهنة للغواة مضادة لله وخروج عن ولايته ، وسبب موجب لغضبه ونكاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage merits reflection that should make a believer kneel, feel fear, and grow firmer in God's religion.
rows.anchor: فعلى المؤمن إذا تلا هذه الآية أن يجثو عندها ويتدبرها

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When the passage was revealed, the Prophet would pray that God not leave him to himself even for an instant.
rows.anchor: اللهم لا تكلني إلى نفسي طرفة عين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of Mecca nearly drove the Prophet from Mecca through hostility and plotting; had they expelled him, God would have destroyed them shortly afterward, as happened at Badr.
rows.anchor: فإن الله مهلكهم وكان كما قال ، فقد أهلكوا ببدر بعد إخراجه بقليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation says that if they had expelled him, they would all have been exterminated.
rows.anchor: وقيل : معناه ولو أخرجوك لاستؤصلوا عن بكرة أبيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpretations take the land as Arabia, or Medina rather than Mecca.
rows.anchor: وقيل : من أرض العرب . وقيل : من أرض المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An account says Jews urged Muhammad to move to Syria, claiming prophets were sent there and Abraham had migrated there; he camped outside Medina before revelation made him return.
rows.anchor: فاجتمعوا إليه وقالوا : يا أبا القاسم ، إن الأنبياء إنما بعثوا بالشام وهي بلاد مقدسة وكانت مهاجر إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading has the verb after kādū coordinated as a raised verb in its predicate; Ubay's reading makes the whole conditional clause coordinate with the preceding clause and uses إذا to govern the verb.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة أبي ( لا يلبثوا ) على إعمال ( إذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has khilāfak; the cited verse of poetry shows khilāf meaning after them.
rows.anchor:
وقرىء ( خلافك ) قال :
عفت الديار خلافهم فكأنما … بسط الشواطب بينهن حصيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The established practice is that God destroys any people who expel their messenger; sunnata is an accusative verbal noun emphasizing that God established this practice.
rows.anchor: أن كل قوم أخرجوا رسولهم من بين ظهرانيهم ، فسنة الله أن يهلكهم ، ونصبت نصب المصدر المؤكد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Duluk may mean sunset or, alternatively, the sun's decline from its zenith; the word is derived from rubbing because one rubs the eye when looking toward the sun.
rows.anchor: دلكت الشمس : غربت . وقيل : زالت

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Gabriel came at the sun's decline and prayed the noon prayer with the Prophet.
rows.anchor: أتاني جبريل عليه السلام لدلوك الشمس حين زالت الشمس . فصلى بي الظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If duluk means zenith, the verse covers all five prayers; if it means sunset, noon and afternoon prayers fall outside its span.
rows.anchor: فإن كان الدلوك الزوال فالآية جامعة للصلوات الخمس ، وإن كان الغروب فقد خرجت منها الظهر والعصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghasaq means darkness and marks the time of the night prayer.
rows.anchor: والغسق : الظلمة ، وهو وقت صلاة العشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'an al-fajr denotes the dawn prayer, naming it for its recitation because recitation is a pillar, like bowing, prostration, and qunūt; this refutes Ibn ʿUlayya and al-Aṣamm's denial that recitation is a pillar.
rows.anchor: سميت قرآنا وهو القراءة ، لأنها ركن ، كما سميت ركوعا وسجودا وقنوتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dawn prayer is witnessed by the angels of night and day, as one group descends while the other ascends; alternatively, many worshippers witness it, or it should be attended by a large congregation.
rows.anchor: يشهده ملائكة الليل والنهار ، ينزل هؤلاء ، ويصعد هؤلاء ؛ فهو في آخر ديوان الليل وأول ديوان النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse may urge lengthy dawn recitation so people hear the Qur'an and its reward increases; dawn is accordingly the longest prayer in recitation.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون { أقم الصلواة } حثا على طول القراءة في صلاة الفجر ، لكونها مكثورا عليها ، ليسمع الناس القرآن فيكثر الثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One grammatical account makes maqāman maḥmūdan an adverb of place or time; another makes ya-bʿathuka mean establish you, and a third makes it a circumstantial phrase meaning one possessing a praised station.
rows.anchor: مقاما محمودا } نصب على الظرف ، أي : عسى أن يبعثك يوم القيامة فيقيمك مقاما محمودا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The praised station is any honored position deserving praise from its occupant and all who see it; intercession is one, narrower interpretation.
rows.anchor: وهو مطلق في كل ما يجب الحمد من أنواع الكرامات ، وقيل : المراد الشفاعة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas describes a station where earlier and later peoples praise Muhammad, who is honored above all creatures, granted requests and intercession, with everyone beneath his banner.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : مقام يحمدك فيه الأولون والآخرون

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet identifies the praised station as the place where he will intercede for his community.
rows.anchor: هو المقام الذي أشفع فيه لأمتي

rows.speaker: حذيفة
rows.claim: Hudhayfa reports that all people will gather on one plain; Muhammad is first called and answers with a prayer declaring that refuge and guidance are with God, identifying this as the praised station.
rows.anchor:
وعن حذيفة
( 629 ) يجمع الناس في صعيد واحد ، فلا تتكلم نفس ، فأول مدعو محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mudkhal and mukhraj are read with either ḍamma or fatḥa, as verbal nouns; the open-vowel reading means God admits and brings the Prophet out with approval and safety.
rows.anchor: قرىء ( مدخل ومخرج ) بالضم والفتح : بمعنى المصدر . ومعنى الفتح : أدخلني فأدخل مدخل صدق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation asks for a truthful, approved entry into the grave and honorable, safe emergence at resurrection, supported by the neighboring mention of resurrection.
rows.anchor: أدخلني القبر مدخل صدق : إدخالا مرضيا على طهارة وطيب من السيئات ، وأخرجني منه عند البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other proposed settings are the Hijra, entering Mecca in conquest and leaving it safely, or entering and leaving the cave unharmed.
rows.anchor: وقيل : نزلت حين أمر بالهجرة ، يريد إدخال المدينة والإخراج من مكة . وقيل : إدخاله مكة ظاهرا عليها بالفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpretations make the prayer about undertaking prophethood and completing its duties without failure, obedience, or generally any matter or place one enters and leaves.
rows.anchor: إدخاله فيما حمله من عظيم الأمر وهو النبوة وإخراجه منه مؤديا لما كلفه من غير تفريط . وقيل : الطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sultan may mean an argument that supports the Prophet against opponents or strong authority that empowers Islam over unbelief.
rows.anchor: سلطانا } حجة تنصرني على من خالفني . أو ملكا وعزا قويا ناصرا للإسلام على الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request for supporting authority was answered by promises of divine protection, the party of God prevailing, Islam's dominance, and the conquest of Persian and Roman kingship.
rows.anchor: فأجيب دعوته بقوله : { والله يعصمك من الناس } ( المائدة : 67 ) . { فإن حزب الله هم الغالبون

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet appointed ʿAttāb ibn Asīd over Mecca; after people objected to his severity, he related a dream of ʿAttāb opening Paradise's gate and said God would strengthen Islam through him.
rows.anchor: أنه استعمل عتاب بن أسيد على أهل مكة وقال ( انطلق فقد استعملتك على أهل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report concludes by identifying ʿAttāb's power to defend Muslims against injustice as the supporting authority requested in the verse.
rows.anchor: فأعز الله به الإسلام لنصرته المسلمين على من يريد ظلمهم ، فذلك السلطان النصير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Kaaba had 360 idols around it, and Ibn Abbas reports that Arab tribes made pilgrimage and sacrifices to their idols there.
rows.anchor: كان حول البيت ثلاثمائة وستون صنما ثم كل قوم بحيالهم . وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : كانت لقبائل العرب يحجون إليها وينحرون لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An account says Gabriel told Muhammad at the conquest to strike the idols while reciting this verse; they fell, and Ali broke the glass idol above the Kaaba as Meccans marveled.
rows.anchor: ولما نزلت هذه الآية يوم الفتح قال جبريل عليه السلام لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : خذ مخصرتك ثم ألقها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Kaaba complained to God that idols were worshipped around it.
rows.anchor: فشكا البيت إلى الله عز وجل فقال : أي رب ، حتى متى تعبد هذه الأصنام حولي دونك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: God answered that He would soon fill the Kaaba with worshippers prostrating, flocking like birds, and calling out in pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: فأوحى الله إلى البيت : إني سأحدث لك نوبة جديدة ، فأملأك خدودا سجدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Truth means Islam, falsehood means polytheism, and falsehood is always destined to disappear.
rows.anchor: والحق : الإسلام . والباطل : الشرك { كان زهوقا } كان مضمحلا غير ثابت في كل وقت

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Zamakhshari calls the Kaaba's complaint to God and the divine answer a figurative personification.
rows.anchor: وشكاية البيت والوحي إليه : تمثيل وتخييل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: God answered that He would soon fill the Kaaba with worshippers prostrating, flocking like birds, and calling out in pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: فأوحى الله إلى البيت : إني سأحدث لك نوبة جديدة ، فأملأك خدودا سجدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Truth means Islam, falsehood means polytheism, and falsehood is always destined to disappear.
rows.anchor: والحق : الإسلام . والباطل : الشرك { كان زهوقا } كان مضمحلا غير ثابت في كل وقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zamakhshari calls the Kaaba's complaint to God and the divine answer a figurative personification.
rows.anchor: وشكاية البيت والوحي إليه : تمثيل وتخييل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb for sending down is read in both the light and doubled forms; min either clarifies the kind or means a portion, in which case every Qur'anic revelation heals believers and improves their religion.
rows.anchor: من للتبيين ، كقوله : { من الاوثان } أو للتبعيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an increases believers' faith and repairs their religion as medicine heals the sick.
rows.anchor: يزدادون به إيمانا ، ويستصلحون به دينهم ، فموقعه منهم موقع الشفاء من المرضى

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet is quoted saying that whoever does not seek healing through the Qur'an will not be healed by God.
rows.anchor:
وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم :
( 632 ) ( من لم يستشف بالقرآن فلا شفاه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an only increases unbelievers' loss because they reject and disbelieve in it.
rows.anchor: ولا يزداد به الكافرون { إلا خسارا } أي نقصانا لتكذيبهم به وكفرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is illustrated by the verse saying that it increased them in defilement upon their defilement.
rows.anchor: كقوله تعالى : { فزادتهم رجسا إلى رجسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When given health and prosperity, a person turns from remembering God as if self-sufficient; turning one's side intensifies the image of arrogance and rejection.
rows.anchor: بالصحة والسعة { أعرض } عن ذكر الله ، كأنه مستغن عنه مستبد بنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When hardship such as poverty, illness, or calamity touches him, he becomes deeply despairing of God's relief.
rows.anchor: من فقر أو مرض أو نازلة من النوازل { كان } شديد اليأس من روح الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading wa-nāʾa bi-jānibihi reverses the positions of the root's lām and ʿayn, like rāʾ in raʾā; it can also derive from nāʾ meaning to rise.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( وناء بجانبه ) بتقديم اللام على العين ، كقوله ( راء ) في ( رأى ) ويجوز أن يكون من ( ناء ) بمعنى ( نهض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each person acts according to a way that suits his condition, whether guidance or error; the branching roads of a path illustrate the sense of shākila.
rows.anchor: على مذهبه وطريقته التي تشاكل حاله في الهدى والضلالة ، من قولهم ( طريق ذو شواكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conclusion is that God knows best who follows the sounder doctrine and path.
rows.anchor: فربكم أعلم بمن هو أهدى سبيلا } أي أسد مذهبا وطريقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most interpreters say the spirit is the spirit within animals; asked about its reality, the Prophet said it is God's command, meaning knowledge God reserved to Himself.
rows.anchor: الأكثر على أنه الروح الذي في الحيوان . سألوه عن حقيقته فأخبر أنه من أمر الله ، أي مما استأثر بعلمه

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن بريدة
rows.claim: Ibn Burayda reports that the Prophet died without knowing the spirit.
rows.anchor:
وعن عبد الله بن بريدة .
( 633 ) لقد مضى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وما يعلم الروح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpretations identify the spirit as a vast spiritual creation greater than an angel, Gabriel, or the Qur'an; on the Qur'an interpretation, God's command means His revelation and speech rather than human speech.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو خلق عظيم روحاني أعظم من الملك . وقيل : جبريل عليه السلام . وقيل : القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Jews told Quraysh to ask about the Sleepers, Dhul-Qarnayn, and the spirit; Muhammad answered the stories but left the spirit's nature obscure, as it was obscure in Torah, and they regretted asking.
rows.anchor: بعثت اليهود إلى قريش أن سلوه عن أصحاب الكهف ، وعن ذي القرنين ، وعن الروح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address in you were given little knowledge is general.
rows.anchor: وما أوتيتم } الخطاب عام

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When asked whether the limited knowledge included only Jews or also the Muslims, the Prophet said it included both.
rows.anchor: فقال : بل نحن وأنتم لم نؤت من العلم إلا قليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection that this contradicts the verse calling wisdom great good is mistaken: greatness and smallness are relative; wisdom is abundant in itself but little beside God's knowledge.
rows.anchor: لأن القلة والكثرة تدوران مع الإضافة ، فيوصف الشيء بالقلة مضافا إلى ما فوقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation addresses the Jews alone because they boasted of Torah wisdom; its knowledge is little compared with God's knowledge.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو خطاب لليهود خاصة ؛ لأنهم قالوا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : قد أوتينا التوراة وفيها الحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sworn conditional threat says God could remove the Qur'an from hearts and manuscripts without leaving a trace, after which none could restore and preserve it.
rows.anchor: ذهبنا بالقرآن ومحوناه عن الصدور والمصاحف فلم نترك له أثرا وبقيت كما كنت لا تدري ما الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Except for God's mercy may be a disconnected exception, meaning that His mercy left the Qur'an with the Prophet rather than removing it.
rows.anchor: أو يكون على الاستثناء المنقطع بمعنى : ولكن رحمة من ربك تركته غير مذهوب به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an's continued preservation follows God's immense favor in revealing and teaching it; scholars should be grateful both for learning that remains in memory and for its continued preservation.
rows.anchor: وهذا امتنان من الله تعالى ببقاء القرآن محفوظا بعد المنة العظيمة في تنزيله وتحفيظه

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud foretells that trust will be the first religious quality lost, prayer the last, and a time when people pray without religion and the Qur'an disappears.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود : : أول ما تفقدون من دينكم الأمانة ، وآخر ما تفقدون الصلاة

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: In response to how the Qur'an could disappear after preservation in hearts and manuscripts and teaching children, Ibn Masud says it will be lifted overnight from manuscripts and hearts.
rows.anchor: فقال : يسرى عليه ليلا فيصبح الناس منه فقراء ترفع المصاحف وينزع ما في القلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge means that even a united humanity and jinn, including eloquent Arabs, cannot match the Qur'an's eloquence, arrangement, and composition.
rows.anchor: لو تظاهروا على أن يأتوا بمثل هذا القرآن في بلاغته وحسن نظمه وتأليفه ، وفيهم العرب العاربة أرباب البيان لعجزوا عن الإتيان بمثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He disputes those who call the Qur'an eternal while admitting its inimitability: inability applies only where the challenged act is possible, whereas a second eternal being is impossible.
rows.anchor: والعجب من النوابت ومن زعمهم أن القرآن قديم مع اعترافهم بأنه معجز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If inability were asserted over what is impossible, one could wrongly describe God as unable; those who claim God can do the impossible merely resort to contradiction.
rows.anchor: فلا يقال للفاعل . قد عجز عنه ، ولا هو معجز ، ولو قيل ذلك لجاز وصف الله بالعجز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣarrafnā means repeatedly circulated or restated, and every mathal means any striking, unusual, or beautiful comparison or meaning.
rows.anchor: صرفنا } رددنا وكررنا { من كل مثل } من كل معنى هو كالمثل في غرابته وحسنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kufūr means denial or ingratitude.
rows.anchor: والكفور : الجحود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception construction is grammatical because abā is understood as negation: they would accept nothing except rejection.
rows.anchor: لأن أبى متأول بالنفي ، كأنه قيل : فلم يرضوا إلا كفورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After being defeated by the Qur'an's inimitability and other proofs, the opponents resorted to demands for signs as a confused, evasive argument.
rows.anchor: لما تبين إعجاز القرآن وانضمت إليه المعجزات الأخر والبينات ولزمتهم الحجة وغلبوا ، أخذوا يتعللون باقتراح الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tafjur means to open or burst forth; a lightened reading is also reported, and yanbūʿ is a continuously flowing spring derived from the root for water welling up.
rows.anchor: تفجر } تفتح . وقرىء ( تفجر ) بالتخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They mean the land of Mecca and demand that a spring flow from it.
rows.anchor: من الارض } يعنون أرض مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qabīlan may mean a guarantor who certifies the claim, someone face-to-face, or a group of angels as a circumstantial phrase.
rows.anchor: كفيلا بما تقول شاهدا بصحته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word qabīlan is illustrated by a poetic line and by the comparison with a verse asking why angels or God are not shown to them.
rows.anchor: أو مقابلا ، كالعشير بمعنى المعاشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demands for gold, heavenly ascent, and a written endorsement were additional conditions; Ibn Abbas attributes the staircase and signed document demand to ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Umayya.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الله بن أبي أمية : لن نؤمن لك حتى تتخذ إلى السماء سلما

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي أمية
rows.claim: He demanded a staircase to heaven, a witnessed ascent, and a signed document from heaven confirming Muhammad's claim.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الله بن أبي أمية : لن نؤمن لك حتى تتخذ إلى السماء سلما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their proposals were stubborn obstruction: even if every sign came, they would call it sorcery, as shown by other rejected miracle proposals.
rows.anchor: وما كانوا يقصدون بهذه الاقتراحات إلا العناد واللجاج ، ولو جاءتهم كل آية لقالوا : هذا سحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qāla subḥāna rabbī is another reading that explicitly makes the messenger the speaker; his wonder at their requests emphasizes that signs belong to God, not to a human messenger.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( قال سبحان ربي ) أي قال الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Like other messengers, Muhammad is only a human messenger; messengers bring their people the signs God manifests, and people cannot dictate those signs.
rows.anchor: وكان الرسل لا يأتون قومهم إلا بما يظهره الله عليهم من الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first in is the second object of manaʿa and the second is its subject; al-huda means revelation, and the objection to human messengers alone held people back from believing in the Qur'an and Muhammad.
rows.anchor: الأولى نصب مفعول ثان لمنع . والثانية رفع فاعل له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their objection is backwards: wisdom dictates that an angel bring revelation only to a similar being or to prophets, and a chosen human then guides other humans.
rows.anchor: لأن قضية حكمته أن لا يرسل ملك الوحي إلا إلى أمثاله ، أو إلى الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If earth were inhabited by angels walking on feet and settled there, God would send them an angel messenger to teach and guide them.
rows.anchor: بأنه { لو كان فى الارض ملائكة يمشون } على أقدامهم كما يمشي الإنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Basharan and malakan can grammatically be read as circumstantial modifiers of rasūlan.
rows.anchor: هل يجوز أن يكون بشرا وملكا ، منصوبين على الحال من رسولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God witnesses that Muhammad delivered his message while his opponents denied and resisted; God knows the messengers and those warned and repays them, consoling the Prophet and threatening unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وهذه تسلية لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ووعيد للكفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shahīdan is parsed either as an accusative of specification or as a circumstantial expression.
rows.anchor: وشهيدا : تمييز أو حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance means God grants success and subtle aid that benefits its recipient; misguidance means He withholds that aid, and no supporter can replace Him.
rows.anchor: ومن يوفقه ويلطف به { فهو المهتدى } لأنه لا يلطف إلا بمن عرف أن اللطف ينفع فيه { ومن يضلل } ومن يخذل

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Asked how people could walk on their faces, the Prophet answered that the One who made them walk on their feet can make them walk on their faces.
rows.anchor: وقيل لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : كيف يمشون على وجوههم قال : ( إن الذي أمشاهم على أقدامهم ، قادر على أن يمشيهم على وجوههم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their blindness, muteness, and deafness continue their worldly refusal to see guidance, speak truth, and hear revelation; they receive nothing pleasing in the next life.
rows.anchor: كما كانوا في الدنيا ، لا يستبصرون ولا ينطقون بالحق ، ويتصامون عن استماعه ، فهم في الآخرة كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, their senses may be intact as they are moved from the gathering place to the Fire after judgment, since another passage says they read and speak.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يحشروا مؤفي الحواس من الموقف إلى النار بعد الحساب ، فقد أخبر عنهم في موضع آخر أنهم يقرؤن ويتكلمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that one blind in this life is blind in the next links the verse to the earlier warning about spiritual blindness.
rows.anchor: ومن كان في هذه أعمى فهو في الآخرة أعمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the Fire's flame subsides after consuming their skin and flesh, replacement bodies are restored and it flares again, repeatedly enacting the resurrection they denied and intensifying regret and punishment.
rows.anchor: كلما خبت } كما أكلت جلودهم ولحومهم وأفنتها فسكن لهبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated consumption and restoration retaliate against their denial of resurrection and deepen their remorse.
rows.anchor: كأنهم لما كذبوا بالإعادة بعد الإفناء جعل الله جزاءهم أن سلط النار على أجزائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase making them an appointed term is coordinated with whether they saw: reason already shows that the creator of heavens and earth can create humans like them.
rows.anchor: على قوله { أو لم * يروا } لأن المعنى قد علموا بدليل العقل أن من قدر على خلق السموات والأرض فهو قادر على خلق أمثالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans are no harder to create than the heavens, and the appointed term means either death or the Resurrection; despite clear evidence, wrongdoers choose denial.
rows.anchor: لأنهم ليسوا بأشد خلقا منهن كما قال : أأنتم أشد خلقا أم السماء { وجعل لهم أجلا لا ريب فيه } وهو الموت أو القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because law normally precedes a verb, the construction implies a repeated tملكون, then replaces the attached subject pronoun with the independent antum for emphasis.
rows.anchor: فلا بد من فعل بعدها في { لو أنتم تملكون } وتقديره لو تملكون تملكون ، فأضمر تملك إضمارا على شريطة التفسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording antum tملكون rhetorically singles people out as especially extreme in miserliness, as illustrated by lines from Hatim and al-Mutalammis.
rows.anchor: أن أنتم تملكون فيه دلالة على الاختصاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mercy treasures mean God's provision and other blessings; Meccans who demanded springs and rivers would themselves hoard those resources if they owned them.
rows.anchor: ورحمة الله : رزقه وسائر نعمه على خلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qatūr means narrow-hearted and miserly; amsaktum has no object because it means simply to be stingy, like calling a miser one who holds back.
rows.anchor: قتورا } ضيقا بخيلا . فإن قلت : هل يقدر { لأمسكتم } مفعول ؟ قلت : لا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas lists the nine signs as staff, hand, locusts, lice, frogs, blood, stone, sea, and the mountain raised over Israel.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : هي العصا ، واليد ، والجراد ، والقمل ، والضفادع ، والدم ، والحجر ، والبحر ، والطور الذي نتقه على بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan instead counts the flood, years of drought, and crop shortages in place of stone, sea, and Mount Sinai.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن : الطوفان ، والسنون ، ونقص الثمرات : مكان الحجر ، والبحر ، والطور

rows.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
rows.claim: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz asked Muhammad ibn Kaʿb, who named the tongue and obliteration; Umar praised his learning and checked a sack of broken food-like stones as evidence.
rows.anchor: وعن عمر بن عبد العزيز أنه سأل محمد بن كعب فذكر اللسان والطمس ، فقال له عمر : كيف يكون الفقيه إلا هكذا

rows.speaker: صفوان بن عسال عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Safwan ibn ʿAssāl reports the Prophet listing nine commands to Moses for Israel: avoid idolatry, theft, adultery, unjust murder, sorcery, usury, false accusations before rulers, slander of chaste women, and fleeing battle; Jews were specially told not to violate the Sabbath.
rows.anchor:
وعن صفوان بن عسال .
( 637 ) أن بعض اليهود سأل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fasʾal banī Isrāʾīl may mean tell Pharaoh to release them, ask Israel about their faith and religion, or ask them to support Moses in mission.
rows.anchor: فقلنا له : سل بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A reading attributed to the Prophet has fa-sāla banī Isrāʾīl, past tense without hamza, in the Quraysh dialect.
rows.anchor: وتدل عليه قراءة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : فسال بني إسرائيل ، على لفظ الماضي بغير همز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Muhammad is told to ask the believing Israelites such as ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam and his companions so their certainty grows through corroborating evidence.
rows.anchor: وقيل : فسل يا رسول الله المؤمنين من بني إسرائيل ، وهم عبد الله بن سلام وأصحابه عن الآيات ليزدادوا يقينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The attachment of idh jāʾahum depends on the interpretation: the omitted command to ask, the non-hamza reading, the bestowal of signs, an implied remember, or an implied they will tell you; the people addressed came to their forefathers.
rows.anchor: فإن قلت : بم تعلق { إذ جاءهم } ؟ قلت : أما على الوجه الأول فبالقول المحذوف ، أي فقلنا لهم سلهم حين جاءهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses tells Pharaoh that he knows the signs came only from God as clear proofs, yet obstinately denies what he knows, as Pharaoh's earlier confirmation shows.
rows.anchor: ما أنزل هؤلاء } الآيات إلا الله عز وجل { بصائر } بينات مكشوفات ، ولكنك معاند ماكبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading with ʿalimtu in the first person has Moses say he knows the signs are true, not that he is bewitched.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( علمت ) بالضم ، على معنى : إني لست بمسحور كما وصفتني ، بل أنا عالم بصحة الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses answers Pharaoh's suspicion with his own, saying Pharaoh is doomed; his judgment rests on visible denial after knowledge, while Pharaoh's accusation is an outright lie.
rows.anchor: ثم قارع ظنه بظنه ، كأنه قال : إن ظننتني مسحورا فأنا أظنك { مثبورا

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains mathbūr as diverted from good and sealed in the heart, from the expression asking what prevented or turned someone away.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء : { مثبورا } مصروفا عن الخير مطبوعا على قلبك ، من قولهم : ما ثبرك عن هذا

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubay ibn Kaʿb reads wa-in akhāluka yā Firʿawnu la-mathbūr, with a lightened in and distinguishing lām.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي بن كعب ( وإن إخالك يا فرعون لمثبورا ) على إن المخففة واللام الفارقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh meant to drive Moses and Israel from Egypt or to eliminate them by killing; God turned the plot back on him by drowning him and his Egyptian followers.
rows.anchor: أن يستخف موسى وقومه من أرض مصر ويخرجهم منها ، أو ينفيهم عن ظهر الأرض بالقتل والاستئصال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israel was told to settle the land Pharaoh had tried to expel them from; the final promise is Resurrection, when all peoples are gathered together and sorted into the blessed and wretched.
rows.anchor: اسكنوا الارض } التي أراد فرعون أن يستفزكم منها { فإذا جاء وعد الاخرة } يعني قيام الساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lafīfan means mixed groups gathered from different tribes.
rows.anchor: جئنا بكم لفيفا } جمعا مختلطين إياكم وإياهم ، ثم يحكم بينكم ويميز بين سعدائكم وأشقيائكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading says the Qur'an was sent down in keeping with the wisdom that called for it and descended bearing truth and guidance to every good; another says it descended guarded by angels from devils' interference.
rows.anchor: وما أنزلنا القرآن إلا بالحكمة المقتضية لإنزاله وما نزل إلا ملتبسا بالحق والحكمة لاشتماله على الهداية إلى كل خير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, revelation descended from heaven in truth under angelic watch and reached the Messenger protected from satanic alteration.
rows.anchor: أو ما أنزلناه من السماء إلا بالحق محفوظا بالرصد من الملائكة ، وما نزل على الرسول إلا محفوظا بهم من تخليط الشياطين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad was sent only to give good news of Paradise and warn of Hell; compulsion into religion and other tasks are beyond his role.
rows.anchor: وما أرسلناك } إلا لتبشرهم بالجنة وتنذرهم من النار ، ليس إليك وراء ذلك شيء ، من إكراه على الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurʾānan is governed by an implied verb explained by farraqnāhu; the light reading signifies close, gradual separation, while the doubled reading means revelation came in installments.
rows.anchor: وقرءانا } منصوب بفعل يفسره { فرقناه } وقرأ أبي ( فرقناه ) بالتشديد ، أي : جعلنا نزوله مفرقا منجما

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas also reads the doubled form and says the revelation spanned twenty years, not just two or three days.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه أنه قرأ مشددا وقال : لم ينزل في يومين أو ثلاثة ، بل كان بين أوله وآخره عشرون سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mukth is read with either fatḥa or ḍamma and means reading at leisure, deliberately, and steadily.
rows.anchor: على مكث } بالفتح والضم : على مهل وتؤدة وتثبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an was sent down in installments in response to unfolding events.
rows.anchor: ونزلناه تنزيلا } على حسب الحوادث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to believe or not believe means disregard and esteem the opponents lightly; if ignorant pagans refuse, learned readers of earlier scripture have recognized the foretold Arab prophet and believe.
rows.anchor: أمر بالإعراض عنهم واحتقارهم والإزدراء بشأنهم ، وأن لا يكترث بهم وبإيمانهم وبامتناعهم عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The learned bow down and glorify God because He fulfilled the promise in their books by sending Muhammad and revealing the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: خروا سجدا وسبحوا الله تعظيما لأمره ولإنجازه ما وعد في الكتب المنزلة وبشر به من بعثه محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fulfilled promise is God's promise and scriptural foretelling of Muhammad's mission and Qur'an.
rows.anchor: وهو المراد بالوعد في قوله : { إن كان وعد ربنا لمفعولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an softens their hearts, moistens their eyes, and increases reverent humility.
rows.anchor: ويزيدهم خشوعا } أي يزيدهم القرآن لين قلب ورطوبة عين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about learned believers may explain the order to believe or not, since better people have believed; alternatively it consoles the Messenger by pointing to the learned converts.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون تعليلا لقوله { به أو لا تؤمنوا إن } وأن يكون تعليلا لقل على سبيل التسلية لرسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Falling on the chin means falling face-first, since the chin is the first part of the face to touch the ground in prostration.
rows.anchor: السقوط على الوجه ، وإنما ذكر الذقن وهو مجتمع اللحيين ، لأن الساجد أول ما يلقى به الأرض من وجهه الذقن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in falling to the chin or face indicates specification or dedication, as illustrated by the poetic phrase of falling prostrate to hands and mouth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording repeats falling to the chins because one fall occurs in prostration and the other while weeping.
rows.anchor: لاختلاف الحالين وهما خرورهم في حال كونهم ساجدين ، وخرورهم في حال كونهم باكين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas relates that Abu Jahl heard Muhammad say Allah and al-Rahman and objected that he forbade worshipping two gods yet called another deity.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما سمعه أبو جهل يقول : يا الله يا رحمن ، فقال : إنه ينهانا أن نعبد إلهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says the People of the Book complained that Muhammad mentioned al-Rahman too little despite its frequent appearance in Torah.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن أهل الكتاب قالوا : إنك لتقل ذكر الرحمن وقد أكثر الله في التوراة هذا الاسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling on the names means naming God, not vocatively supplicating Him; the verb can take two objects, though one may be omitted.
rows.anchor: والدعاء بمعنى التسمية لا بمعنى النداء ، وهو يتعدى إلى مفعولين ، تقول : دعوته زيدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allah and al-Rahman denote the names; whichever one is used, all the beautiful names belong to their referent, God Himself.
rows.anchor: والله والرحمان ، المراد بهما الاسم لا المسمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conjunction offers a choice of either name; tanwin in ayyā replaces its genitive complement and mā emphasizes the generality of which name is used.
rows.anchor: وأو للتخيير ، فمعنى { ادعوا الله أو ادعوا الرحمان } سموا بهذا الاسم أو بهذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun to Him refers to the named divine essence, not either name; the two names are beautiful because they express praise, sanctification, and greatness.
rows.anchor: والضمير في { فله } ليس براجع إلى أحد الاسمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer here means its recitation by ellipsis; the Prophet raised his voice and pagans abused him, so he was told to lower it enough to avoid them but not hide it from followers.
rows.anchor: بصلاتك بقراءة صلاتك على حذف المضاف ؛ لأنه لا يلبس

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Abu Bakr prayed quietly, saying he was confiding in his Lord who knew his need; Umar prayed loudly to repel Satan and wake sleepers, so both were told to moderate.
rows.anchor: وروي أن أبا بكر رضي الله عنه كان يخفي صوته بالقراءة في صلاته ويقول : أناجي ربي

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Umar said that he raised his voice to repel Satan and wake the sleeper.
rows.anchor: وكان عمر رضي الله عنه يرفع صوته ويقول : أزجر الشيطان وأوقظ الوسنان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation says not to recite every prayer either loudly or quietly, but to recite night prayers aloud and daytime prayers softly.
rows.anchor: وقيل : معناه ولا تجهر بصلاتك كلها ولا تخافت بها كلها ، وابتغ بين ذلك سبيلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer may instead mean supplication; some scholars considered this verse abrogated by the command to call upon God humbly and privately.
rows.anchor: وقيل { بصلاتك } بدعائك . وذهب قوم إلى أن الآية منسوخة بقوله : { ادعوا ربكم تضرعا وخفية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking a middle way is a figure for choosing a moderate manner of recitation.
rows.anchor: وابتغاء السبيل : مثل لانتحاء الوجه الوسط في القراءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Walī min al-dhull can mean a helper and protector against humiliation, or that God needs no ally whose loyalty would ward off humiliation.
rows.anchor: ولى من الذل } ناصر من الذل ومانع له منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Praising God after denying child, partner, and humiliation is apt because only one with these attributes can bestow every blessing and deserves all praise.
rows.anchor: لأن من هذا وصفه هو الذي يقدر على إيلاء كل نعمة ، فهو الذي يستحق جنس الحمد

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet taught this verse to a boy from Banu Abd al-Muttalib as soon as the child could speak clearly.
rows.anchor: وكان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أفصح الغلام من بني عبد المطلب علمه هذه الآية

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises a qintar in Paradise to whoever reads Surat Banī Isrāʾīl and is moved at its mention of parents; a qintar is given as 1,200 uqiyyas.
rows.anchor:
عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم .
( 640 ) ( من قرأ سورة بني إسرائيل فرق قلبه عند ذكر الوالدين كان له قنطار في الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is Meccan except verse 38 and verses 83–101, which are Medinan; it has 110 verses and followed al-Ghāshiya in revelation.
rows.anchor:
مكية ( إلا آية 38 ومن آية 83 إلى غاية آية 101 فمدنية )
وآياتها 110 ( نزلت بعد الغاشية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God teaches His servants to praise Him for Islam, their greatest blessing, and the Book revealed to Muhammad that brings salvation and success.
rows.anchor: لقن الله عباده وفقههم كيف يثنون عليه ويحمدونه على أجزل نعمائه عليهم وهي نعمة الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the Book wholly free of crookedness; for meanings, crookedness means contradiction or anything departing from wisdom and correctness.
rows.anchor: ولم يجعل له شيئا من العوج قط ، والعوج في المعاني كالعوج في الأعيان ، والمراد نفي الاختلاف والتناقض عن معانيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qayyiman is best parsed with an implied verb rather than as a circumstantial modifier, avoiding separation from its noun by part of the relative clause; absence of crookedness thereby establishes uprightness.
rows.anchor: الأحسن أن ينتصب بمضمر ولا يجعل حالا من الكتاب ؛ لأن قوله { ولم يجعل } معطوف على أنزل ، فهو داخل في حيز الصلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pairing the denial of crookedness with the assertion of uprightness emphasizes perfection, since an apparently straight thing might still show subtle defects under close inspection.
rows.anchor: فائدته التأكيد ، فرب مستقيم مشهود له بالاستقامة ولا يخلو من أدنى عوج عند السبر والتصفح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other readings of qayyiman make the Book a confirmer and witness of other scriptures, or one that directs people's interests and necessary laws.
rows.anchor: وقيل : قيما على سائر الكتب مصدقا لها ، شاهدا بصحتها . وقيل : قيما بمصالح العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anẓara takes two objects, but only the severe punishment is expressed because it is the intended focus; the warned people are specified separately in verse 4.
rows.anchor: أنذر ) متعد إلى مفعولين ، كقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: From His presence means issued from God Himself.
rows.anchor: من لدنه } صادرا من عنده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good reward promised to believers is Paradise, where they remain forever.
rows.anchor: والأجر الحسن : الجنة { ما لهم به من علم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good reward promised to believers is Paradise, where they remain forever.
rows.anchor: والأجر الحسن : الجنة { ما لهم به من علم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who say God has a son have no knowledge of this claim; it comes from extreme ignorance, inherited imitation, and Satan's deception.
rows.anchor: ما لهم به من علم } أي بالولد أو باتخاذه ، يعني أن قولهم هذا لم يصدر عن علم ولكن عن جهل مفرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lack of knowledge either reflects ignorance of a way to know or the claim's impossibility, since knowledge cannot attach to an impossible thing.
rows.anchor: لأنه ليس مما يعلم لاستحالته ، وانتفاء العلم بالشيء إما للجهل بالطريق الموصل إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kaburat is read with kalimatan in accusative as specification or kalimatu in nominative as subject; accusative is stronger and carries an exclamatory sense.
rows.anchor: قرىء ( كبرت كلمة ) ، وكلمة : بالنصب على التمييز والرفع على الفاعلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase describing the word coming from their mouths magnifies their effrontery: people suppress even private evil thoughts, but these people dare utter this monstrous claim.
rows.anchor: تخرج من أفواههم } صفة للكلمة تفيد استعظاما لاجترائهم على النطق بها وإخراجها من أفواههم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has the bāʾ of kaburat quiescent with a trace of ḍamma; its subject is the claim that God took a son, called a word as a poem may be called a word.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( كبرت ) بسكون الباء مع إشمام الضمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who debated the Sleepers' number around Muhammad asked him, and revelation foretold their future disagreement; the accurate view is seven and their dog eighth, with Ibn Abbas counting himself among the few who know.
rows.anchor: الضمير لمن خاض في قصتهم في زمن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من أهل الكتاب والمؤمنين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says he is one of the few who know the Sleepers' number.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنه : أنا من أولئك القليل

rows.speaker: السيد والعاقب
rows.claim: In a report about Christians from Najran with the Prophet, the Jacobite leader says three and the Nestorian leader says five, while the Muslims say seven; God confirms the Muslims' number, learned from Gabriel's revelation.
rows.anchor: فقال السيد وكان يعقوبيا : كانوا ثلاثة رابعهم كلبهم

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali names the seven sleepers, their positions among King Decianus's advisers, the shepherd who joined them, their city Ephesus, and their dog's name Qitmir.
rows.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه : هم سبعة نفر أسماؤهم : يمليخا ، ومكشليتيا ، ومشلينيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The future sīn may scope over both later statements, or the imperfect verbs may themselves carry future meaning.
rows.anchor: فإن قلت : لم جاء بسين الاستقبال في الأول دون الآخرين ؟ قلت : فيه وجهان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rajman bil-ghayb means throwing out hidden information, like the Qur'anic use of throwing something in the unseen.
rows.anchor: رجما بالغيب } رميا بالخبر الخفي وإتيانا به كقوله { ويقذفون بالغيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rajm may be idiomatic for supposition because Arabs used rajm al-ẓann so often for guessing; Zuhayr's line uses it for a conjectured account.
rows.anchor: أو وضع الرجم موضع الظن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word in Zuhayr's citation means conjectured; another reading merges the thāʾ of thalāth with the feminine tāʾ.
rows.anchor: أي المظنون . وقرىء ( ثلاث رابعهم ) بإدغام الثاء في تاء التأنيث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Three, five, and seven predicate omitted they; each following phrase about their dog is a clause describing that number.
rows.anchor: ثلاثة } خبر مبتدأ محذوف ، أي : هم ثلاثة . وكذلك { خمسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conjunction waw appears before the third description because a descriptive clause may take waw, which reinforces its attachment and the stable, confident quality of the claim.
rows.anchor: هي الواو التي تدخل على الجملة الواقعة صفة للنكرة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says that once the waw appears, the count stops; no further number needs consideration.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنه : حين وقعت الواو انقطعت العدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the few who know to be a small number of the People of the Book; most of them only guess.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إلا قليل من أهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not argue about the Sleepers beyond what revelation states; present it plainly without humiliating or scolding the People of the Book, following the command to debate graciously.
rows.anchor: فلا تجادل أهل الكتاب في شأن أصحاب الكهف إلا جدالا ظاهرا غير متعمق فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not question them either to trap them or to seek instruction, because God has already revealed the story.
rows.anchor: ولا تسأل أحدا منهم عن قصتهم سؤال متعنت له ، حتى يقول شيئا فترده عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-haqq is the predicate of an omitted subject; truth has removed the excuses, leaving people to choose the route of salvation or destruction, as though ordered to choose between paths.
rows.anchor: الحق خبر مبتدأ محذوف . والمعنى : جاء الحق وزاحت العلل فلم يبق إلا اختياركم لأنفسكم ما شئتم من الأخذ في طريق النجاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire's surrounding enclosure may be a tent's curtain-like structure, smoke surrounding unbelievers, or a wall of fire around them.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو دخان يحيط بالكفار قبل دخولهم النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hot drink's m-hal is melted minerals from the earth; another view takes it as sediment from oil.
rows.anchor: والمهل : ما أذيب من جواهر الأرض . وقيل : دردي الزيت

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet describes the drink as oil dregs; its heat burns the face when brought near, making the facial skin fall away.
rows.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم هو كعكر الزيت ، فإذا قرب إليه سقطت فروة وجهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description of the Fire as a foul resting place echoes the following verse's good resting place for Paradise's people, although the damned have no actual place to recline.
rows.anchor: وهذا لمشاكلة قوله { وحسنت مرتفقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poetic line is offered as another use of the word for reclining or propping oneself up.
rows.anchor: إني أرقت فبت الليل مرتفقا … كأن عيني فيها الصاب مذبوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ulaika may be the predicate of inna while the inna lā nuḍīʿ clause is parenthetical; alternatively both are predicates, or ulaika begins an explanation of the unspecified reward.
rows.anchor: أولائك } خبر إن و { إنا لا نضيع } اعتراض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If inna lā nuḍīʿ is the predicate, its missing pronoun is supplied by man ahsana ʿamalan, which has the same meaning as those who believe and act righteously.
rows.anchor: من أحسن عملا } و { الذين ءامنوا وعملوا الصالحات } ينتظمهما معنى واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bracelets are left indefinite to suggest their beautiful nature is beyond description.
rows.anchor: وتنكير { أساور } لإبهام أمرها في الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first min introduces the bracelets' material and the second describes it.
rows.anchor: من الأولى للابتداء . والثانية للتبيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sundus is fine silk and istabraq is thick silk, combining both kinds.
rows.anchor: وجمع بين السندس : وهو مارق من الديباج ، وبين الإستبرق : وهو الغليظ منه ، جمعا بين النوعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reclining is chosen as the posture of prosperous people and kings on their couches.
rows.anchor: وخص الاتكاء ، لأنه هيئة المنعمين والملوك على أسرتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parable compares unbelievers and believers with two brothers, one disbelieving and one believing.
rows.anchor: أي ومثل حال الكافرين والمؤمنين ، بحال رجلين وكانا أخوين في بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account names the Israelite brothers Qatros, the unbeliever, and Yahudha, the believer; they inherited eight thousand dinars and divided it equally.
rows.anchor: أحدهما كافر اسمه قطروس ، والآخر مؤمن اسمه يهوذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view identifies them with the companion pair mentioned in al-Saffat.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هما المذكوران في سورة والصافات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In an illustrative story, the believing brother spends four thousand dinars on heavenly equivalents of land, home, spouse, and servants, donating each thousand; when needy he meets his wealthy brother, who rebukes and drives him away.
rows.anchor: فاشترى الكافر أرضا بألف ، فقال المؤمن : اللهم إن أخي اشترى أرضا بألف دينار ، وأنا أشتري منك أرضا في الجنة بألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative identification makes the brothers Makhzumites: the believer is Abu Salama, later husband of Umm Salama before Muhammad, and the unbeliever is al-Aswad ibn Abd al-Asad.
rows.anchor: مؤمن وهو أبو سلمة عبد الله بن عبد الأشد ، وكان زوج أم سلمة قبل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two grape gardens are ringed by date palms with crops between them, an arrangement landowners use to border vineyards with fruit trees.
rows.anchor: وحففناهما بنخل } وجعلنا النخل محيطا بالجنتين ، وهذا مما يؤثره الدهاقين في كرومهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction describes one connected, carefully arranged estate of crops and fruit, with complete harvests and abundant river water.
rows.anchor: ووصف العمارة بأنها متواصلة متشابكة لم يتوسطها ما يقطعها ويفصل بينها ، مع الشكل الحسن والترتيب الأنيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akl means fruit and lam tazlim means the harvest suffered no diminution.
rows.anchor: والأكل : الثمر . وقرىء ( بضم الكاف ) { ولم تظلم } ولم تنقص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular verb atat agrees with the singular form of kilta; the dual atata would also be valid by agreement with its meaning.
rows.anchor: وآتت : حمل على اللفظ ، لأن { كلتا } لفظه لفظ مفرد ، ولو قيل : آتتا على المعنى : لجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden verb has a lightened reading, and Abdullah reads kull al-jannatayn with the verb and pronoun agreeing with kull.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( وفجرنا ) على التخفيف وقرأ عبد الله ( كل الجنتين آتى أكله ) برد الضمير على كل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamar means multiple kinds of wealth; Mujahid says the man had gold and silver in addition to the two gardens, making him wealthy enough to develop land as he pleased.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد : الذهب والفضة ، أي : كانت له إلى الجنتين الموصوفتين الأموال الدثرة من الذهب والفضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nufr may mean supporters and retinue, or sons because they accompany their father unlike daughters; yuhāwiruhu means exchanging speech.
rows.anchor: وأعز نفرا } يعني أنصارا وحشما . وقيل : أولادا ذكورا ، لأنهم ينفرون معه دون الإناث ، يحاوره : يراجعه الكلام
